entries.description:
Start a background monitor that streams events from a long-running script. Each stdout line is an event — you keep working and notifications arrive in the chat. Events arrive on their own schedule and are not replies from the user, even if one lands while you're waiting for the user to answer a question.

Pick by how many notifications you need:
- **One** ("tell me when the server is ready / the build finishes") → use **Bash with `run_in_background`** and a command that exits when the condition is true, e.g. `until grep -q "Ready in" dev.log; do sleep 0.5; done`. You get a single completion notification when it exits.
- **One per occurrence, until the monitor expires (re-arm to continue)** ("tell me every time an ERROR line appears") → Monitor with an unbounded command (`tail -f`, `inotifywait -m`, `while true`).
- **One per occurrence, until a known end** ("emit each CI step result, stop when the run completes") → Monitor with a command that emits lines and then exits.

Your script's stdout is the event stream. Each line becomes a notification. Exit ends the watch.

  # Each matching log line is an event
  tail -f /var/log/app.log | grep --line-buffered "ERROR"

  # Each file change is an event
  inotifywait -m -q --format '%e %f' /watched/dir

  # Poll GitHub for new PR comments and emit one line per new comment
  last=$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)
  while true; do
    now=$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)
    gh api "repos/owner/repo/issues/123/comments?since=$last" --jq '.[] | "\(.user.login): \(.body)"'
    last=$now; sleep 30
  done

  # Node script that emits events as they arrive (e.g. WebSocket listener)
  node watch-for-events.js

  # Per-occurrence with a natural end: emit each CI check as it lands, exit when the run completes
  prev=""
  while true; do
    s=$(gh pr checks 123 --json name,bucket)
    cur=$(jq -r '.[] | select(.bucket!="pending") | "\(.name): \(.bucket)"' <<<"$s" | sort)
    comm -13 <(echo "$prev") <(echo "$cur")
    prev=$cur
    jq -e 'all(.bucket!="pending")' <<<"$s" >/dev/null && break
    sleep 30
  done

**Don't use an unbounded command for a single notification.** `tail -f`, `inotifywait -m`, and `while true` never exit on their own, so the monitor stays armed until timeout even after the event has fired. For "tell me when X is ready," use Bash `run_in_background` with an `until` loop instead (one notification, ends in seconds). Note that `tail -f log | grep -m 1 ...` does *not* fix this: if the log goes quiet after the match, `tail` never receives SIGPIPE and the pipeline hangs anyway.

**Script quality:**
- Every pipe stage must flush per line or matches sit in its buffer unseen: `grep` needs `--line-buffered`, `awk` needs `fflush()`. `head` cannot flush at all — `| head -N` delivers nothing until N matches accumulate, then ends the stream.
- In poll loops, handle transient failures (`curl ... || true`) — one failed request shouldn't kill the monitor.
- Poll intervals: 30s+ for remote APIs (rate limits), 0.5-1s for local checks.
- Write a specific `description` — it appears in every notification ("errors in deploy.log" not "watching logs").
- Only stdout is the event stream. Stderr goes to the output file (readable via Read) but does not trigger notifications — for a command you run directly (e.g. `python train.py 2>&1 | grep --line-buffered ...`), merge stderr with `2>&1` so its failures reach your filter. (No effect on `tail -f` of an existing log — that file only contains what its writer redirected.)

**Coverage — silence is not success.** When watching a job or process for an outcome, your filter must match every terminal state, not just the happy path. A monitor that greps only for the success marker stays silent through a crashloop, a hung process, or an unexpected exit — and silence looks identical to "still running." Before arming, ask: *if this process crashed right now, would my filter emit anything?* If not, widen it.

  # Wrong — silent on crash, hang, or any non-success exit
  tail -f run.log | grep --line-buffered "elapsed_steps="

  # Right — one alternation covering progress + the failure signatures you'd act on
  tail -f run.log | grep -E --line-buffered "elapsed_steps=|Traceback|Error|FAILED|assert|Killed|OOM"

For poll loops checking job state, emit on every terminal status (`succeeded|failed|cancelled|timeout`), not just success. If you cannot confidently enumerate the failure signatures, broaden the grep alternation rather than narrow it — some extra noise is better than missing a crashloop.

**Output volume**: Every stdout line is a conversation message, so the filter should be selective — but selective means "the lines you'd act on," not "only good news." Never pipe raw logs; filter to exactly the success and failure signals you care about. Monitors that produce too many events are automatically stopped; restart with a tighter filter if this happens.

Stdout lines within 200ms are batched into a single notification, so multiline output from a single event groups naturally.

The script runs in the same shell environment as Bash. Exit ends the watch (exit code is reported). Every monitor expires after `timeout_ms` (default 5 minutes, at most 30 minutes): it is killed and you get one notice with the event count. Re-arm it if you still need the watch; for a long watch (PR monitoring, log tails) set `timeout_ms` to the maximum and re-arm on each expiry, and widen the filter if an expiry with no events was unexpected. Use TaskStop to cancel early.
**ws source** — open a WebSocket and stream each incoming text frame as an event. No shell, no polling: the server pushes, you get notified.

  Monitor({
    ws: {url: 'wss://events.example.com/stream', protocols: ['v1']},
    description: 'deploy events',
  })

Each text frame becomes one notification (multiline frames stay as one event). Binary frames are reported as `[binary frame, N bytes]` rather than passed through. Socket close ends the watch with the close code surfaced; errors are surfaced before close. Same rate limiting as bash — a firehose will be suppressed and eventually stopped, so subscribe to a filtered feed where one exists.

Prefer this over `command: 'websocat wss://…'` — it avoids the extra process and line-buffering pitfalls. Use bash when you need to transform or filter frames with shell tools before they become events.

command.description: Shell command or script. Each stdout line is an event; exit ends the watch.

description.description: Short human-readable description of what you are monitoring (shown in notifications).

timeout_ms.description: Kill the monitor after this deadline. Default 300000ms. Deadlines above 1800000ms are capped to 1800000ms. You are notified at expiry and can re-arm.

ws.description: WebSocket to open. Each text frame is an event; binary frames are reported as a placeholder line. Socket close ends the watch. Cannot be combined with command.

<result>## AI Game Developer (ai-game.dev): facts from the pages

**Bottom line for a Three.js 0.180 + Spark project:** the pages I read say the product supports Three.js, but none of them describe how it works with an existing Three.js project, which tools the agent gets for Three.js, or whether it runs headless on Linux. Those are "not stated" below. The only Three.js-specific statements are marketing lines.

### (1) What it is, and engine support

- **Desktop app plus CLI, with a hosted MCP endpoint.** The download page offers a desktop app (Windows x64, macOS Apple silicon and Intel, Linux x86_64) and a CLI installed with `npm install -g @baizor/gamedev`. Source: https://ai-game.dev/download and https://ai-game.dev/docs/wiki/app/installation
- **Also an MCP server.** It is hosted at `https://ai-game.dev/mcp`, using Streamable HTTP. Source: https://ai-game.dev/mcp-endpoint-info
- **Engine plugins.** Unity, Unreal and Godot plugins are installed by the app or CLI, and they are the engines with an MCP tool count (72, 98 and 47). Source: https://ai-game.dev/docs/wiki/app/projects-and-engines
- **Not a cloud IDE.** Nothing I read describes a browser IDE. The homepage calls it "a free desktop app."
- **Three.js wording, exact:**
  - Homepage, "Six engines, one app": "plus BRUTAL, Bevy and Three.js, which the app creates, builds and runs for you."
  - FAQ: the app and CLI "also create and run BRUTAL (C#, .NET 10), Bevy (Rust; install Rust with rustup) and Three.js web games, and connect the agent to the running game."
  - Homepage step 2: "Pick a new or existing Unity, Unreal, Godot, BRUTAL, Bevy or Three.js project."
  - Sources: https://ai-game.dev/ and https://ai-game.dev/ FAQ section
- **Three.js is absent from the engine-specific docs.** The supported-engines table on https://ai-game.dev/docs/wiki/app/projects-and-engines lists only Unity, Unreal and Godot. Three.js has no install guide, no MCP setup command and no Three.js tool list in any page I read. Its Three.js page was not linked from the pages I read.

### (2) Existing project, or only new ones?

- **Existing projects are claimed, but not detailed.** The homepage says to pick "a new or existing" Three.js project. Nothing says whether a Vite/TypeScript project, or a standalone HTML page using three.js 0.180 and @sparkjsdev/spark with .glb models, is detected or supported.
- **Any folder can be opened.** The projects page says: "You can also open any other folder... The agent can then work with files, packages and tools, just without engine tools." Whether a Three.js folder counts as an "engine tools" case is not stated.
- **Create and open flows** (for Unity, Unreal and Godot only, per the same page): "Open folder…" in the app, or `gamedev /path/to/your/game` in the CLI.

### (3) How it connects to Claude Code

- **Command, from https://ai-game.dev/mcp-endpoint-info:** `claude mcp add --transport http ai-game-dev "https://ai-game.dev/mcp"`
- **Auth:** OAuth 2.1 browser sign-in. A personal access token can be used instead, via an `Authorization: Bearer` header.
- **Project pinning:** `/mcp/p/<pin>` is pinned to one project. It is written by `setup-mcp`, which exists only for `unity-mcp-cli`, `unreal-mcp-cli` and `godot-cli`. No Three.js equivalent is documented.
- **Tool names for Three.js:** not stated. The only published names are examples, such as "Screenshot / Isolated GameObject" and "Console / Get Logs" (Godot). The full catalogue is at https://ai-game.dev/docs/tools, which I did not fetch.
- **Playtest and input features** (screenshot, input events, video recording, scene graph, transforms, materials): not stated for Three.js. The homepage says the agent "enters Play mode, reads console errors and takes screenshots" (Unity/Unreal/Godot context).

### (4) Linux and headless

- **Linux desktop:** AppImage and .deb, x86_64 only. "No arm64 Linux build yet." Source: https://ai-game.dev/docs/wiki/app/installation
- **CLI on Linux:** prebuilt binaries for x64 and arm64. It needs Node.js 22 or newer. Note that the download page says "Node.js 20.19+ or 22.12+", which does not match the installation page.
- **Headless mode exists for prompts, not rendering.** `gamedev --print "<prompt>"` and `--headless` send a prompt and print the reply. The CLI reference does not say the game is rendered headless. Source: https://ai-game.dev/docs/wiki/app/cli
- **Software WebGL, display requirements, GPU requirements for the game:** not stated.
- **Browser extension:** none mentioned.
- **Account needed:** yes. "On first launch the CLI asks you to sign in." This also applies on the Free plan.
- **Hosted dependency:** the app and CLI require sign-in to the hosted service. The Free plan works with your own agent, but prompts go straight to your provider. Paid AI goes through their servers.

content.text:
I don't recommend adopting AI Game Developer, Thrixel Build World, or any of the earlier three tools. Nothing I found suggests any of them can bring Screen 05 closer to your approved picture than what we already have. Nothing was installed, no accounts were created, no money or credits were spent, and your artwork wasn't uploaded anywhere.

**AI Game Developer (ai-game.dev)**
- **Your Three.js project:** its Three.js support was announced six days ago and is documented only for new games built from its own starter projects. Opening an existing project gets one marketing line and no instructions. It never mentions the 3D-capture technology your Screen 05 world is built from (Gaussian splats, drawn by the Spark library).
- **What it would add:** it claims screenshots, scene inspection, touch input and pass/fail playtests. We already run all of these here: real finger swipes on an Android portrait screen, a screenshot every frame, Benny's position and the camera read from the live game, and automatic checks. It doesn't claim to compare the game against a reference picture, which we already do.
- **What it is underneath:** its command-line tool is built on the same Claude agent I am, so it wouldn't see the differences any better.
- **Cost and privacy:** even the free plan needs an account sign-in, and paid plans are $25–199 a month.

**Thrixel Build World** generates new 3D models with AI, which is the new interpretation you've ruled out. We tested it once in round 19, with your sign-in, on Screen 04's foam, and it was not an improvement.

**onGame** and **SceneSim** don't turn up anywhere under those names. If you have links, send them and I'll check.

**Cuberta and Scenario YVO3D:**
- **Cuberta** builds roads, buildings and terrain from its own kit pieces and runs only on Windows or Mac. Under its maker's terms, free outputs belong to them and are non-commercial.
- **Scenario YVO3D** paints new textures with AI and is designed for single objects, not tunnels. It may also use your uploads to improve its models.

**The actual obstacle** is that your approved Screen 05 is one painting from one viewpoint. While Benny swims and moves left and right, the game has to show walls, river bends and sides the painting never shows. Every tool above fills those gaps with AI-generated art or its own kit, so none of them solves this.

**What I'd do instead:**
1. **Finish the current Screen 05 build.** A short test is running now: 7.6 seconds of swimming with real left, right, up and down swipes. When it finishes I'll check it for glitches, black patches, flicker, Benny tilting or leaving the river, and colour likeness to your picture, then fix what fails. I won't show you a preview that doesn't pass.
2. **Build a tunnel kit from your original painting's pixels.** It would have separate pieces for the ring section, the purple perforated wall, the gold rings and the S-shaped river, with textures cut and repeated from your painting itself, not repainted by AI. That keeps the tunnel sharp along the whole level and is lighter on Android phones. Our Blender specialist can build it for free. """Round 33 kit: fit ONE straight tunnel with evenly spaced gold rings to the approved Screen 05 painting (camera at origin, fov 64).
Camera coords: x right, y up, looking down -z. Unknowns: axis direction (via vanishing point vx, vy), camera offset from the axis
(ox, oy, tunnel radius = 1), depth t2 of painted ring 2 along the axis, ring spacing S. Objective: blurred gold coverage along each
predicted ring (rings 2..7, upper 260 deg only: the bottom is under the river). Writes tunnel_fit.json."""
import sys, json, numpy as np, cv2
from scipy.optimize import minimize
gold = np.load(sys.argv[1]).astype(np.float32); H, W = gold.shape
gold[:230] = 0; gb = cv2.GaussianBlur(gold, (0, 0), 3)
FOC = (H / 2) / np.tan(np.radians(64) / 2)
def axis_from_vp(vx, vy):
    a = np.array([(vx - W / 2) / FOC, -(vy - H / 2) / FOC, -1.0]); return a / np.linalg.norm(a)
def basis(a):
    up = np.array([0, 1.0, 0]); n = up - a * (up @ a); n /= np.linalg.norm(n); r = np.cross(a, n); return n, r
def proj(P):
    z = -P[..., 2]; return W / 2 + FOC * P[..., 0] / z, H / 2 - FOC * P[..., 1] / z, z
TH = np.radians(np.linspace(-40, 220, 160))      # angle from the tunnel's right, counter-clockwise (top = 90)
def ring_pts(p, k):
    vx, vy, ox, oy, t2, S = p; a = axis_from_vp(vx, vy); n, r = basis(a)
    C = ox * r + oy * n + (t2 + (k - 2) * S) * a
    P = C[None] + np.cos(TH)[:, None] * r[None] + np.sin(TH)[:, None] * n[None]
    return proj(P)
def score(p, ks=range(2, 8)):
    tot = 0
    for k in ks:
        x, y, z = ring_pts(p, k); ok = (z > 0.05) & (x >= 0) & (x < W - 1) & (y >= 230) & (y < H - 1)
        if ok.sum() < 10: continue
        tot += gb[y[ok].astype(int), x[ok].astype(int)].mean() * (1 + 0.15 * (7 - k))
    return -tot
if __name__ == '__main__':
    # start: VP (504, 449); ring 2 radius 246 px => t2 = FOC / 246 (radius 1); camera offset from ring-centre drift (-0.137, +0.042 in px-y)
    p0 = np.array([504, 449, 0.137, -0.042, FOC / 246, FOC / 151 - FOC / 246])
    best = None
    for jit in range(12):
        st = p0 * (1 + (np.random.default_rng(jit).normal(0, 0.04, 6) if jit else 0))
        res = minimize(score, st, method='Nelder-Mead', options={'maxiter': 3000, 'xatol': 1e-3, 'fatol': 1e-5})
        if best is None or res.fun < best.fun: best = res
    p = best.x; print('fit', np.round(p, 4), 'score', -best.fun)
    for k in range(1, 11):
        x, y, z = ring_pts(p, k); top = np.argmin(np.abs(TH - np.pi / 2))

"""Round 33 kit: fit ONE straight tunnel with evenly spaced gold rings to the approved Screen 05 painting (camera at origin, fov 64).
Camera coords: x right, y up, looking down -z. Unknowns: axis direction (via vanishing point vx, vy), camera offset from the axis
(ox, oy, tunnel radius = 1), depth t2 of painted ring 2 along the axis, ring spacing S. Objective: blurred gold coverage along each
predicted ring (rings 2..7, upper 260 deg only: the bottom is under the river). Writes tunnel_fit.json."""
import sys, json, numpy as np, cv2
from scipy.optimize import minimize
gold = np.load(sys.argv[1]).astype(np.float32); H, W = gold.shape
gold[:230] = 0; gb = cv2.GaussianBlur(gold, (0, 0), 3)
FOC = (H / 2) / np.tan(np.radians(64) / 2)
def axis_from_vp(vx, vy):
    a = np.array([(vx - W / 2) / FOC, -(vy - H / 2) / FOC, -1.0]); return a / np.linalg.norm(a)
def basis(a):
    up = np.array([0, 1.0, 0]); n = up - a * (up @ a); n /= np.linalg.norm(n); r = np.cross(a, n); return n, r
def proj(P):
    z = -P[..., 2]; return W / 2 + FOC * P[..., 0] / z, H / 2 - FOC * P[..., 1] / z, z
TH = np.radians(np.linspace(-40, 220, 160))      # angle from the tunnel's right, counter-clockwise (top = 90)
def ring_pts(p, k):
    vx, vy, ox, oy, t2, S = p; a = axis_from_vp(vx, vy); n, r = basis(a)
    C = ox * r + oy * n + (t2 + (k - 2) * S) * a
    P = C[None] + np.cos(TH)[:, None] * r[None] + np.sin(TH)[:, None] * n[None]
    return proj(P)
def score(p, ks=range(2, 8)):
    tot = 0
    for k in ks:
        x, y, z = ring_pts(p, k); ok = (z > 0.05) & (x >= 0) & (x < W - 1) & (y >= 230) & (y < H - 1)
        if ok.sum() < 10: continue
        tot += gb[y[ok].astype(int), x[ok].astype(int)].mean() * (1 + 0.15 * (7 - k))
    return -tot

    p0 = np.array([504, 449, 0.137, -0.042, FOC / 246, FOC / 151 - FOC / 246])
    best = None

        res = minimize(score, st, method='Nelder-Mead', options={'maxiter': 3000, 'xatol': 1e-3, 'fatol': 1e-5})
        if best is None or res.fun < best.fun: best = res
    p = best.x; print('fit', np.round(p, 4), 'score', -best.fun)

        ok = (z > 0.05) & (x >= 0) & (x < W) & (y >= 230) & (y < H)

"""Bake the Screen 05 tunnel kit textures from the ORIGINAL approved pixels (round 33). No AI, no repainting: every texel is a
bilinear sample of references/05_flow_into_the_current.png at the place where the kit surface lands in the approved camera view
(through the same depth curve the game uses). Only where Benny / coins / star / HUD cover the scenery does the round-32 clean plate
(same picture with those removed, pixel-aligned: median difference 1-3 levels elsewhere) fill in.
  python3 -I bake_kit.py <outdir>
Writes wall.png (periodic: one ring-to-ring section, all copies share it), ring.png (front face + inner face of a gold ring),
river.png (the water surface, log-spaced along the tunnel), kit.json (geometry for kit05.html), and coverage maps for the report."""
import sys, json, numpy as np, cv2
from PIL import Image
sys.path.insert(0, __import__('os').path.dirname(__import__('os').path.abspath(__file__)))
from kit_model import *

out = sys.argv[1]; os.makedirs(out, exist_ok=True)
ref = np.array(Image.open(os.path.join(REPO, 'references/05_flow_into_the_current.png')).convert('RGB')).astype(np.float32)
cln = np.array(Image.open(os.path.join(REPO, 'qa/worldlabs/05/r32/input_05_clean.png')).convert('RGB').resize((W, H), Image.LANCZOS)).astype(np.float32)
cover = (np.abs(ref - cln).mean(2) > 30).astype(np.uint8)
cover[:205] = 1                                                     # HUD bar + title (and the repainted rows behind them)
cover = cv2.dilate(cover, np.ones((9, 9), np.uint8))
src = np.where(cover[..., None] > 0, cln, ref)                        # original pixels, clean plate only under Benny / coins / HUD
srcm = cv2.GaussianBlur(src, (0, 0), 0.6)                             # tiny pre-blur against aliasing in the farther samples

def sample(x, y):
    return cv2.remap(srcm, x.astype(np.float32), y.astype(np.float32), cv2.INTER_LINEAR, borderMode=cv2.BORDER_REPLICATE)

TH0, TH1 = np.radians(-50), np.radians(230)                          # wall above the water: sin(theta) > -HW/RT (-45.6 .. 225.6 deg)
RINGS = range(-2, 40)

def hidden_by_ring(t):
    """wall at axial t (seen from the start camera, approx. on the axis) is behind a gold ring band"""
    gt = g(t); h = np.zeros(t.shape, bool)
    for j in RINGS:
        tj = ring_t(j)
        if tj <= 0.05: continue
        gj = g(tj); h |= (t > tj) & (gt <= gj * RT / RING_IN)
    return h

def best_of(copies, P_of, extra_ok=None):
    """for every texel take the copy seen largest (nearest) in the approved picture where it is visible"""
    shp = None; best_d = None; best_x = best_y = None
    for c in copies:

+    return best_x, best_y, np.isfinite(best_d), best_d
+
+# ---------------- wall: periodic tile, theta x one ring spacing ----------------
+TW, TH_ = 2048, 1024
+th = np.linspace(TH0, TH1, TW)[None, :].repeat(TH_, 0)
+u = (np.arange(TH_)[:, None] + 0.5) / TH_ * S * np.ones((1, TW))      # 0 .. S behind the ring's front face
+def wall_P(k): return wall_point(th, ring_t(k) + u)
+wx, wy, wok, wd = best_of(range(1, 12), wall_P, lambda k, P: ~hidden_by_ring(np.asarray(P) @ A))
+wall = sample(wx, wy); wall[~wok] = 0
+# texels never visible (e.g. low on the walls, behind foam): fill from the neighbours along the tunnel / around it
+fill = (~wok).astype(np.uint8)
+wall8 = np.clip(wall, 0, 255).astype(np.uint8)
+if fill.any(): wall8 = cv2.inpaint(wall8, fill, 5, cv2.INPAINT_TELEA)
+Image.fromarray(wall8).save(os.path.join(out, 'wall.png'))
+src_k = np.zeros(wok.shape, np.uint8)
+for k in range(1, 12):
+    x, y, z = project(wall_P(k)); src_k[np.isclose(wx, x) & wok] = k
+Image.fromarray((src_k * 20).astype(np.uint8)).save(os.path.join(out, 'wall_sourcecopy.png'))
+print('wall: visible texels', round(float(wok.mean()), 3), 'copies used', np.bincount(src_k[wok].ravel(), minlength=12)[1:].tolist())
+
+# ---------------- gold ring: v 0..0.5 front face (outer -> inner), 0.5..1 inner face (front -> back) ----------------
+RW_, RH_ = 2048, 160
+thr = np.linspace(TH0, TH1, RW_)[None, :].repeat(RH_, 0)
+v = (np.arange(RH_)[:, None] + 0.5) / RH_ * np.ones((1, RW_))
+def ring_P(k):
+    front = v < 0.5; rad = np.where(front, RT - (RT - RING_IN) * (v / 0.5), RING_IN); tt = ring_t(k) + np.where(front, 0.0, (v - 0.5) / 0.5 * RING_W)
+    return wall_point(thr, tt, 1.0) * 0 + A0 + tt[..., None] * A + rad[..., None] * (np.cos(thr)[..., None] * RR + np.sin(thr)[..., None] * NUP)
+rx, ry, rok, rd = best_of(range(1, 12), ring_P)
+ring = sample(rx, ry); ring8 = np.clip(ring, 0, 255).astype(np.uint8)
+if (~rok).any(): ring8 = cv2.inpaint(ring8, (~rok).astype(np.uint8), 5, cv2.INPAINT_TELEA)
+Image.fromarray(ring8).save(os.path.join(out, 'ring.png'))
+print('ring: visible texels', round(float(rok.mean()), 3))
+
+# ---------------- water surface (river + foam banks), not periodic: lateral x log-spaced axial t ----------------
+HWD = float(np.sqrt(RT ** 2 - HW ** 2)); T0, T1 = 0.25, 60.0
+VW, VH = 1024, 4096
+lat = np.linspace(-HWD, HWD, VW)[None, :].repeat(VH, 0)
+tv = T0 * (T1 / T0) ** ((np.arange(VH)[:, None] + 0.5) / VH) * np.ones((1, VW))
+Pw = A0 + tv[..., None] * A + lat[..., None] * RR - HW * NUP
+x, y, z = project(Pw); ok = (z > 0.05) & (x >= 0) & (x < W - 1) & (y >= 0) & (y < H - 1)
+water = sample(np.clip(x, 0, W - 1), np.clip(y, 0, H - 1)); water8 = np.clip(water, 0, 255).astype(np.uint8)
+if (~ok).any(): water8 = cv2.inpaint(water8, (~ok).astype(np.uint8), 5, cv2.INPAINT_TELEA)
+Image.fromarray(water8[::-1]).save(os.path.join(out, 'river.png'))      # row 0 = far end (texture v = 1 at the top)
+print('water: visible texels', round(float(ok.mean()), 3), 'half width', round(HWD, 3))
+
+kit = export(); kit.update({'TH0': TH0, 'TH1': TH1, 'water': {'T0': T0, 'T1': T1, 'HWD': HWD}, 'textures': ['wall.png', 'ring.png', 'river.png'],
+            'benny_start_px': [432, 1180], 'fov': SC['cam']['fov'], 'cam_fwd': F.tolist(), 'cam_up': U.tolist()})
+json.dump(kit, open(os.path.join(out, 'kit.json'), 'w'), indent=1)
+print('wrote', out)

+"""Round 33: APPROVED | CURRENT (round-32 splat build) | KIT, measured the same way.
+python3 -I compare_r33.py <current run dir> <kit run dir> <outdir> [frames=0,15,30]
+Frame 0 = the approved camera in both builds, so it is compared pixel by pixel with the approved picture (scaled to the 412 x 915 phone
+frame: same vertical field of view, sides cropped). Scenery = everything below the HUD minus a generous box around Benny (both builds
+use the same Benny model, so he is not part of the scenery comparison). Later frames have no approved counterpart (the camera has moved):
+for them the colour look (hue/saturation histogram correlation with the approved scenery) and sharpness (Laplacian energy relative to the
+approved) are reported, plus the pictures."""
+import sys, os, json, numpy as np, cv2
+from PIL import Image
+cur, kit, out = sys.argv[1:4]; frames = [int(x) for x in (sys.argv[4] if len(sys.argv) > 4 else '0,15,30').split(',')]
+os.makedirs(out, exist_ok=True)
+REF = os.path.join(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)), '..', '..', 'references', '05_flow_into_the_current.png')
+W, H = 412, 915
+ref = Image.open(REF).convert('RGB'); sc = H / ref.height; rw = round(ref.width * sc)
+ref = np.array(ref.resize((rw, H), Image.LANCZOS))[:, (rw - W) // 2:(rw - W) // 2 + W].astype(np.float32)
+mask = np.ones((H, W), bool); mask[:125] = False; mask[400:780, 50:362] = False     # HUD rows; Benny box
+def load(d, i): return np.array(Image.open(os.path.join(d, f'f_{i:04d}.jpg')).convert('RGB').resize((W, H))).astype(np.float32)
+def ssim(a, b):
+    a = cv2.cvtColor(a.astype(np.uint8), cv2.COLOR_RGB2GRAY).astype(np.float32); b = cv2.cvtColor(b.astype(np.uint8), cv2.COLOR_RGB2GRAY).astype(np.float32)
+    k = lambda x: cv2.GaussianBlur(x, (0, 0), 1.5); ma, mb = k(a), k(b); va, vb, cab = k(a * a) - ma ** 2, k(b * b) - mb ** 2, k(a * b) - ma * mb
+    C1, C2 = (0.01 * 255) ** 2, (0.03 * 255) ** 2; return ((2 * ma * mb + C1) * (2 * cab + C2)) / ((ma ** 2 + mb ** 2 + C1) * (va + vb + C2))
+def hs_corr(a, b):
+    def h(x): hsv = cv2.cvtColor(x.astype(np.uint8), cv2.COLOR_RGB2HSV); m = mask.astype(np.uint8); hh = cv2.calcHist([hsv], [0, 1], m, [36, 16], [0, 180, 0, 256]); return cv2.normalize(hh, hh).flatten()
+    return float(cv2.compareHist(h(a), h(b), cv2.HISTCMP_CORREL))
+def sharp(x): g = cv2.cvtColor(x.astype(np.uint8), cv2.COLOR_RGB2GRAY).astype(np.float32); return float(np.abs(cv2.Laplacian(g, cv2.CV_32F))[mask].mean())
+res = {'rule': 'scenery = below the HUD, Benny box excluded; frame 0 compared pixel by pixel with the approved picture', 'frames': {}}
+s_ref = sharp(ref)
+for i in frames:
+    row = {}
+    for name, d in (('current', cur), ('kit', kit)):
+        try: im = load(d, i)
+        except FileNotFoundError: continue
+        r = {'colour_look_corr': round(hs_corr(im, ref), 3), 'sharpness_vs_approved': round(sharp(im) / s_ref, 3)}
+        if i == 0:
+            diff = np.abs(im - ref).mean(2)
+            r.update({'mean_abs_diff_levels': round(float(diff[mask].mean()), 1), 'share_within_20_levels': round(float((diff[mask] < 20).mean()), 3),
+                      'ssim_scenery': round(float(ssim(im, ref)[mask].mean()), 3)})
+        row[name] = r
+    res['frames'][str(i)] = row
+    ims = [ref] + [load(d, i) for d in (cur, kit) if os.path.exists(os.path.join(d, f'f_{i:04d}.jpg'))]
+    sheet = np.full((H, W * len(ims) + 12 * (len(ims) - 1), 3), 255, np.uint8)
+    for j, im in enumerate(ims): sheet[:, j * (W + 12):j * (W + 12) + W] = im.astype(np.uint8)
+    Image.fromarray(sheet).save(os.path.join(out, f'APPROVED_CURRENT_KIT_f{i:04d}.jpg'), quality=92)
+json.dump(res, open(os.path.join(out, 'compare_r33.json'), 'w'), indent=1); print(json.dumps(res, indent=1))

   is an orange smear, Benny banks to ~30 deg and slides partly off-screen on a left lane change, lilac smear in the lower water.
   Root cause found: the Marble world's rings and its water plane do NOT line up with the painting (water plane tilted: a tunnel
   parallel to it would put the vanishing point 138 px above the painted core).
3. NEW METHOD — tunnel kit from the ORIGINAL pixels (`tools/kit05/`), user's plan step 3:
   * `kit_model.py`: ONE straight tunnel, evenly spaced gold rings, fitted to the painted rings (ring tops within ~5 px for rings 2,3,5-8,
     8 px ring 4; sides within ~10 px). The painting is not strict perspective: from ring 2 inward each ring is ~1.52x deeper than the
     previous (constant ratio). Every scenery vertex goes through a camera-relative depth curve g() along the tunnel axis: identity up to
     ring 2 (Benny, his water, controls = plain 3D), exponential beyond (the painting's ring ratio from EVERY camera position; like the
     "curved world" shaders of endless runners). Water plane parallel to the axis, camera 0.734 above it (round-32 scale).
   * `bake_kit.py`: wall (periodic ring-to-ring tile), gold ring, water textures = bilinear samples of the APPROVED picture where the
     surface lands in the approved camera view (no AI). Hidden spots: walls → round-32 clean plate (last resort, penalised x4);
     water → the user's ORIGINAL isolated water art (`references/water/05_water_isolated_original.png`, colour-matched).
   * `kitgame.html` (= play3.html-compatible page): kit scenery + the round-32 Benny + UNCHANGED `controls.js` (swipes, lanes, leap, dive,
     coins, splash, camera springs) → runs in the existing acceptance harness `tools/marble05/viewer/final_acceptance.cjs`.
4. Short-section test (first 7.6 s of the level, fixed swipe plan L L R U R R D L U L, real CDP touch, 412x915 Android portrait):
   10/10 swipes ok, lanes -1/0/+1, no teleports (max 0.041/frame), up/down smooth (max 0.067/frame), camera smooth, 0 errors,

input.content:
# Round 33 report — Screen 05: tools evaluated, new tunnel-kit method tested and adopted for the full level (2026-11-21)

Session branch `ccr-81d66c17-i0ooo8`. Nothing installed, no account created, no credits or money spent, approved artwork unchanged
(`sha256sum -c scripts/reference.sha256`). Experimental work only in `/tmp/rainbow_r33` + `tools/kit05/` (new files); the round-32
build, `controls.js`, Benny and every protected branch are untouched.

## 1. Tools the user asked about — none adopted
`TOOL_EVALUATION_R33.md`: Cuberta (Windows/macOS kit-piece city builder; free outputs owned by Wandy3D), Scenario YVO3D (AI re-texturing,
single objects, may train on uploads), SceneSim / onGame (not found), AI Game Developer (Three.js support only for new projects from its
own starters, same Claude agent underneath, its screenshot / touch / playtest features already exist here), Thrixel Build World
(generative; tested in round 19: not an improvement). None can reproduce the ORIGINAL pixels; none was installed.

## 2. Why the round-32 splat world could not reach the approved look
* Its rings do not sit on the painted rings, and its water plane is tilted against the painted tunnel (a tunnel parallel to it puts the
  vanishing point 138 px above the painted core). Splats from one picture also blur within ~2-3 s of swimming.
* The painting itself is not drawn in strict perspective: from ring 2 inward every gold ring is ~1.52x deeper than the previous one.

## 3. The tunnel kit (user's plan step 3) — `tools/kit05/`
* ONE straight 3D tunnel with evenly spaced gold rings fitted to the painted rings (ring tops within ~5 px for rings 2, 3, 5-8).
* A camera-relative depth curve (identity up to ring 2, then the painting's ring ratio) applied to every scenery vertex, so the far
  tunnel keeps the painted perspective from every position (the "curved world" technique of endless-runner games).
* Textures = the APPROVED pixels themselves (bilinear samples where each surface lands in the approved camera view):
  per-section own pixels for the first 8 wall sections + 9 rings (exact painting at the start), cross-faded to a sharp shared section
  as Benny approaches; water = the approved water, flowing into a seamless current made from the user's isolated water art + the
  approved near water; foam banks = the painting's own foam. AI-made pixels (round-32 clean plate) only as a last resort on walls.
* Gameplay = the round-32 Benny + UNCHANGED `controls.js` (lanes, leap, dive, coins, splash, camera springs); bank softened through
  its own tuning switch (`c_LEAN_K` 0.20 -> 0.11).

## 4. Short-section test (first 7.6 s, fixed swipe plan L L R U R R D L U L, real touch, 412 x 915 Android portrait)
| scenery (HUD + Benny box excluded) | CURRENT splat | KIT (own pixels) |
|---|---|---|
| frame 0: share within 20 levels of approved | 12.7 % | **80.0 %** |
| frame 0: mean abs difference | 60.5 | **14.6** |
| frame 0: SSIM | 0.19 | **0.76** |
| frame 0: colour-look correlation | 0.55 | **0.99** |
| frame 0: sharpness vs approved | 0.30 | **0.75** |
| frames 15 / 30 (swimming, steering): colour look | 0.36 / 0.25 | **0.71 / 0.73** |
| frames 15 / 30: sharpness | 0.34 / 0.36 | **0.60 / 0.64** |
| render time per frame (software WebGL) | ~25 s | **~2.5 s** |
Gameplay in the same test: 10/10 swipes answered (4 left, 3 right, 2 up, 1 down), lanes -1 / 0 / +1, no teleports (max 0.041 per
frame), up / down smooth (max 0.067 per frame), camera smooth, 0 errors. Evidence: `qa/kit05/r33/`.
=> Meaningfully better than the current version without damaging gameplay → extended to the full Screen 05 (user's rule).

## 5. Honest limits (not yet solved)
* 80 % of scenery pixels within 20 levels at the start, not 90-95 %: remaining differences are mostly coin positions (the controls'
  coin layout vs the painted coins), the far river, and Benny (the 3D Benny model is ~28 % wider than the painted Benny — character
  work, not scenery).
* While swimming, the river beyond the painted stretch runs straight between foam banks; the painting's winding S-shape is only in the
  painted stretch. Paddles (gold lids) are flat on the walls, not 3D.
* No physical Android device or emulator here: tests use Chromium's Android-portrait emulation with real touch events; frame rate on a
  phone cannot be measured here (the kit is ~10x lighter to render than the splat world, a good sign, not a measurement).

## 6. Commissioning a specialist instead?
Not needed for the tunnel itself: the kit already reproduces the approved tunnel from its own pixels. A human 3D artist would only be
